links.outcome: Accuracy of optometrists' glaucoma referral decisions with versus without AI, and AI alone
links.effect: Human-AI teams achieved higher accuracy (60%) than humans alone (51%), but underperformed the AI alone (80% accuracy); explanations did not enhance performance.
links.quote: In a user study with 87 optometrists, human-AI teams achieved higher accuracy (60%) than humans alone (51%), but explanations did not enhance performance.

links.outcome: Over-reliance on incorrect AI recommendations and anchoring bias with explanations
links.effect: Post-hoc explanations increased over-reliance on incorrect AI recommendations, and both explanation types contributed to anchoring bias, aligning participants more closely with AI referrals.
links.quote: Post-hoc explanations increased over-reliance on incorrect AI recommendations, and both explanation types contributed to anchoring bias, making participants align more closely with AI referrals than without explanations.

links.outcome: Effect of intrinsic and post-hoc AI explanations on user performance and trust calibration
links.effect: Explanations did not enhance performance, introduced uncertainty about when to trust AI, and post-hoc explanations increased over-reliance on incorrect AI recommendations.
links.quote: Instead, they introduced uncertainty about when to trust AI.
